_notes: v1.6.0 (2026-08, Phase 86): PreToolUse carries `timeout: 600` (Claude
Code's per-hook timeout, seconds). Its default is 60s, while the
desktop Gate waits up to 120s (600 clamp) for the human - so Claude
Code was killing the hook before the answer came back. The CLI
writes `timeout` through only when a spec entry has one. Existing
machines must re-run setup-hooks to pick it up.
v1.2.0 (2026-07): dropped Notification + SessionStart — observability-only
noise (the agent is driven by the main session, not by these alerts).
Only actionable lifecycle signals remain: Stop ('your turn') and
SessionEnd ('session closed'). Stale settings.json entries that still
call `claude-hook notification|session-start` are silent-acked by the
CLI. Lifecycle matchers are the empty string — the documented
'applies always' form ('*' is a literal, not a wildcard). This syncs
the github spec with the CLI's bundled v1.2.0 (cli/src/hooks.rs).
v1.5.0 (2026-08, Phase 84.B): Notification is BACK, and this is a
deliberate partial reversal of v1.2.0 above. It was noise as a FEED
ITEM - a card per event that nobody ever acted on. It is the only
signal Claude Code emits for 'the agent is blocked on the human',
which is the red light on a pane tab / pane header. The CLI filters
on notification_type (permission_prompt, idle_prompt,
agent_needs_input, elicitation_dialog, elicitation_url_dialog ->
needs-input; elicitation_complete/_response -> running; anything
else, including a type added upstream later, exits before any RPC)
and pushes the TYPE ALONE - never notification_text, which is
agent/user prose. The desktop routes it to per-pane state and
returns early, so it never becomes a feed item or a toast.
The matcher is the empty string rather than per-type matchers: the
CLI has to read notification_type anyway, one entry beats five, and
an unknown type then logs and no-ops instead of silently never
firing. Existing machines MUST re-run setup-hooks to get red -
green and yellow ride hooks that are already registered.
v1.4.0 (2026-08): the winmux -> ymux rename. Every command now expands
${YMUX_BIN} and resolves to ~/.ymux/bin/ymux, so settings.json files
written against the old path must be re-synced — hence the bump. The
CLI still expands a leftover ${WINMUX_BIN} and treats an entry naming
either binary as its own, so the re-sync replaces rather than
duplicates.
v1.3.0 (2026-08, issue #4): added UserPromptSubmit as the turn-start
signal for the ymux-tools chrome Ticker. It fires in every permission
mode (unlike pre-tool-use, which the CLI short-circuits in
acceptEdits/bypass). The desktop keeps it OFF the feed — no card, no
toast — it only stamps per-pane turn timing (rpc_server.rs feed.push).
Existing machines must re-run setup-hooks to pick it up.
UserPromptSubmit also seeds the STABLE session name (Phase 81.F):
on a session's first real prompt the CLI derives
'<two words> · <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM>' into session-meta.json as
`auto_name`, and returns it as the display title from then on (it
beats the churning claude_title). No spec change was needed — this
rides the v1.3.0 registration above, so machines already set up do
NOT need to re-run setup-hooks.
PreToolUse: fires BEFORE Claude Code invokes a tool. Returning
permissionDecision=allow/deny/ask is the only way to gate a tool.
Claude Code only blocks on the hook when permission_mode is the
default 'plan'/'default' mode; if the user has flipped to
acceptEdits / bypassPermissions / skip, the tool runs regardless,
so ymux's `pre-tool-use` short-circuits with allow in those modes
(otherwise the user would see a dead card they can't act on).
Stop: fires when the assistant finishes a turn. ymux uses it to
trigger the optional Claude auto-summary (Phase 17) and to update
the server-side session-meta map (Phase 81: tmux session ->
claude_session_id + title in ~/.ymux/session-meta.json).
SessionEnd: teardown; Phase 81 prunes dead sessions from the map.
The PreToolUse matcher is intentionally narrow — restricting which
tools surface a ymux card. Override with `--matcher-mode all` (or
Settings → Hooks → 'Match all tools') to route EVERY tool through
ymux. Use `custom` if you've hand-edited ~/.claude/settings.json
and don't want setup-hooks to overwrite the matchers.
